react_result.final_narrative_text: The eight differentially abundant metabolites converge overwhelmingly on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA (KEGG:map00380, FDR 7.8×10⁻¹³), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (KEGG:hsa00380, p=5.5×10⁻⁶), and Mummichog m/z-direct activity (MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism, p=2.5×10⁻⁴) — tryptophan metabolism ranks as the top hit in every analysis. Five input metabolites map to this pathway: L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), serotonin (KEGG:C00780), melatonin (KEGG:C01598), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632), and quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722). This span covers the full kynurenine-branch output (3-HAA, quinolinic acid → NAD⁺ precursor) and the serotonin-to-melatonin branch, indicating coordinated dysregulation of both major tryptophan catabolic arms. Supporting the serotonin/melatonin branch, Reactome pathway R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) achieves FDR 9.1×10⁻⁹ (RaMP rank 5). NAD⁺-centric relevance is further reinforced by WP:WP4210 (Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD⁺ production, RaMP rank 1, FDR 2.95×10⁻¹¹) and WP:WP5414 (IDO metabolic pathway, FDR 3.96×10⁻⁹), both of which include quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. Two metabolites — O-phosphoethanolamine and 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutaric acid — map to phospholipid / glyoxylate metabolism branches and show weaker, single-tool enrichment (Mummichog ranks 3–4). 3-Methyladenine appears in the purine metabolism periphery (Mummichog rank 9). The dominant biological story is therefore a central tryptophan catabolism shift, likely involving IDO/kyurenine pathway activation, with downstream consequences for neurotransmitter (serotonin/melatonin) and NAD⁺ biosynthetic pools.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment tools converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant signal. RaMP multi-database ORA ranks KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) first with FDR 7.8×10⁻¹³, and WikiPathways WP:WP4210 (Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production) second with FDR 2.95×10⁻¹¹. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirms KEGG:hsa00380 at p=5.49×10⁻⁶. Mummichog m/z-direct activity independently returns Tryptophan metabolism as its top hit (p=1.68×10⁻⁴), providing cross-paradigm replication across ORA, PSEA, and network-activity paradigms. The enrichment covers both tryptophan catabolic arms: the serotonin-to-melatonin branch (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin in KEGG:map00380 and REACT:R-HSA-209931 Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) and the kynurenine-to-NAD+ branch (L-tryptophan, quinolinic acid, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid in WP:WP4210 and WP:WP3645 NAD+ biosynthetic pathways). Five driver metabolites are verified members of KEGG:map00380 and four are verified members of WP:WP4210. O-Phosphoethanolamine, 3-methyladenine, and 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutaric acid show only single-tool enrichment and are not driver metabolites in the consensus view.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The eight differentially abundant metabolites converge overwhelmingly on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA (KEGG:map00380, FDR 7.8×10⁻¹³), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (KEGG:hsa00380, p=5.5×10⁻⁶), and Mummichog m/z-direct activity (MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism, p=2.5×10⁻⁴) — tryptophan metabolism ranks as the top hit in every analysis. Five input metabolites map to this pathway: L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), serotonin (KEGG:C00780), melatonin (KEGG:C01598), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632), and quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722). This span covers the full kynurenine-branch output (3-HAA, quinolinic acid → NAD⁺ precursor) and the serotonin-to-melatonin branch, indicating coordinated dysregulation of both major tryptophan catabolic arms. Supporting the serotonin/melatonin branch, Reactome pathway R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) achieves FDR 9.1×10⁻⁹ (RaMP rank 5). NAD⁺-centric relevance is further reinforced by WP:WP4210 (Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD⁺ production, RaMP rank 1, FDR 2.95×10⁻¹¹) and WP:WP5414 (IDO metabolic pathway, FDR 3.96×10⁻⁹), both of which include quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. Two metabolites — O-phosphoethanolamine and 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutaric acid — map to phospholipid / glyoxylate metabolism branches and show weaker, single-tool enrichment (Mummichog ranks 3–4). 3-Methyladenine appears in the purine metabolism periphery (Mummichog rank 9). The dominant biological story is therefore a central tryptophan catabolism shift, likely involving IDO/kyurenine pathway activation, with downstream consequences for neurotransmitter (serotonin/melatonin) and NAD⁺ biosynthetic pools.
